title: Jumpr - Wagertech Next Steps

items.topic: Start fresh, do not reuse existing code
items.statement: The existing org already has over 8,000 lines of code. WagerTech confirmed the earlier proof-of-concept build is not usable, and both sides agreed to start fresh without reusing the existing code.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: I think we're all very aligned that uh the implementation that we've done so far, although it did help prove the concept is not usable or or best practice. / Waleed Alasadi: So go faster. Okay. Okay. All right. So basically the summary is um like I think we want to start fresh for the most part like we don't we don't want to use any of the code that you have existing

items.statement: Jumpr recommended a native-first approach (flows, standard layouts, Lightning web components in native pages) instead of custom code, to support growth and avoid reliance on a single developer. WagerTech accepted this.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: So when we talk about the nativity of Salesforce, it's really about being able to use their automation systems non-codebased the layouts that they've provided um flows. / Emily Vandenberg: That makes sense.

items.statement: Using WhatsApp as the place where rep work is captured (for example API integration or reading chats with N8N) is not part of Phase 1 and needs a separate conversation. WagerTech agreed.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: So, I think that that deserves another conversation. Um, and it aligns with kind of what you expected in that Um, in the beginning, this is not going to be part of phase one. / Joyce Kiddell: Totally.

items.statement: Joyce suggested that the PRD notifications and alerting section could pivot from native Salesforce app or email notifications to WhatsApp. Waleed said this could happen; the notification automation lives in Salesforce and an app may be needed to send to WhatsApp. No final decision was made.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: So like even though initially I think we were thinking like maybe that's like native in the Salesforce app or like email for example, maybe that like we pivot that to just be like WhatsApp focused. / Waleed Alasadi: So and that that could happen absolutely like notifications to WhatsApp could happen.

items.statement: For notifications only, one WhatsApp Business account that sends notifications is enough; reps would not need to switch their personal accounts. Lina said WagerTech could get a dedicated WhatsApp Business account for this. No commitment was made.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: the if we're only sending notifications, then we only need the the one account that would be sending / Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, we could get a WhatsApp business account dedicated to this. / Waleed Alasadi: Okay, perfect.

items.topic: Person accounts for players and referrers
items.statement: Jumpr proposed Person Accounts for both players and referrers instead of B2B account plus contact. Waleed stated this is not final and the design will be finalized in about the first week.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: However, we think for for you guys, this is the that like it cannot be more perfect for the use case that you have for both players and referers. So, we can talk more about like this is not final. Obviously, in the first like week or so, we're going to finalize the design.

items.topic: Native User object for reps and managers
items.statement: Jumpr proposed dropping the custom rep and manager objects in the current PRD/org and using the native User object instead.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Um, we saw that you created like objects for reps, objects for managers. Um, we don't need any of that. I think we should just stick to the user like native user object which could handle all of your kind of like requirements within there.

items.topic: Operator and partner as Accounts; market custom
items.statement: Jumpr proposed that operator and partner are Account records (allowing account hierarchy later) and that market is a custom object.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Um, the operator is an account, the partner is an account. / Waleed Alasadi: Uh market is custom. It's going to be like very straightforward, but it is custom.

items.statement: Jumpr endorsed WagerTech's deal rep assignment object as the key to automating book assignment and monitoring reps, and to moving off Airtable. Deal stays as WagerTech designed it.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Uh market is custom. It's going to be like very straightforward, but it is custom. It allows you flexibility in the future. Um deal is what you have. This deal rep assignment I think is genius.

items.topic: Sign-up intake flow and email matching
items.statement: Proposed flow: the API sends the sign-up and creates a Sign-Up record; the system checks the email. Unknown email creates a Lead (unverified player); known email matches the sign-up to the existing player Person Account. Sign-ups would no longer be leads converted to contacts.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: So right now you have signups as leads and then converting into contacts. Um we we don't want really that to happen. / Waleed Alasadi: It's going to create the signup record and then say, "Do I know this email address? Do I not know this email address?" If it does not know the email address, then it's going to create a lead. / Waleed Alasadi: Um, if we do know the player, then it just kind of matches the sign up to the existing player in the system, which as I said earlier is going to be this person account.

items.statement: The trigger for converting a Lead to a player Person Account is not decided; likely after first deposit proof is verified.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Um, and then, um, if they are a lead, once we have like I don't know, we're gonna have to decide when that action happens, but likely once they send proof for the first deposit or what have you, once we verify they're a player, the system will convert them to a to a player or a person account.
items.critic_note: summary_agreement changed to no: Gemini Details says the workflow 'was defined' and conversion happens once verification such as depositing funds completes; transcript says the conversion trigger is still to be decided.

items.statement: Jumpr proposed a payout line item object (not in WagerTech's design) so each payout amount can be traced and the books closed.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: you didn't have payout line item but I think that the payout especially seeing that you do go and pay like wonderfer you go and give them 2600 bucks like where did that 2600 bucks come from right just so that you close the books on all the the gaps

items.statement: Jumpr proposed an automatically maintained bank transfer object to show a ledger of player bank transactions. Joyce confirmed it is right to have it in Phase 2.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: So it's just um an automated it would be an automated maintain an automatically maintained object. / Joyce Kiddell: Uh, but either way, that's like a a down the line conversation. So, it's right that you have it in phase two, but I like that you're already thinking about that.

items.statement: WagerTech is exploring fintech payment processors that could integrate with Salesforce; Joyce called this a down-the-line conversation. Waleed said the bank transfer object could interact with the processor (draft, sent to processor, result back to Salesforce).
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: I didn't have it on there yet because we were exploring potential like payment processing like fintech solutions that could potentially directly integrate with Salesforce. Uh, but either way, that's like a a down the line conversation. / Waleed Alasadi: Okay, I love that you said that choice because this object too could be the one that is interacting with your payment processor.

items.statement: Lina asked to include an API connection with WagerTech's current bank in scope discussion. Jumpr has never connected to a bank and did not agree; it will research and get back.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: We're also looking to explore the API connection with our current bank. So that's something to discuss in this scope too. / Waleed Alasadi: Um I know it's possible to connect with banks. We have never connected with banks before. So we'll need to I feel I can just imagine how much like requirements there would be. Um so we'll have to get back to you on that one.
items.critic_note: summary_agreement changed to no: Gemini Details attributes the bank API interest to Joyce; transcript shows Lina asked (line 192).

items.statement: Jumpr will research connecting Salesforce to WagerTech's current bank via API and report back to Lina.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Okay. Let's uh we can do some research and get back to you, Lena, on what we know.

items.topic: Data engineer ERD as source of truth
items.statement: WagerTech asked that its data engineer's ERD be the source of truth, with Jumpr and the data engineer finalizing the object design together and the data engineer owning the final outlook. Waleed agreed; finalizing this design is the first week's work if the engagement proceeds.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: diagram if you're familiar with that. So, our hope is that like we use that as kind of the source of truth, / Joyce Kiddell: but like together the two of you kind of work on like if this goes through um what the final state looks like because he'll have some thoughts, you guys can have some thoughts, but ultimately like we want him to be able to own that kind of final outlook just because he's trying to prep it for like connecting um other data sources as well. / Waleed Alasadi: Yeah, absolutely. And that that would that would be what we look forward to in the first week is just finalizing that design with kind of whoever your representatives are.

items.statement: Phase 1 is proposed as building the object model, having sign-ups flow in from the API, and completing the first sign-up flow.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: So the first one is just really building the object model making sure that the signups flow in uh properly from the from the API um and then being able to kind of complete that first signup flow.

items.statement: WagerTech asked for mid-July. Waleed said mid-July is really tight even with two resources and put end of July as the proposed date. The date was not agreed in this meeting.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: I know you mentioned middle of July. It is really tight to be able to go middle of July if we're going to assign two resources to be able to kind of get it done. um with a very aggressive I think July 31st or end of July.

items.statement: Phase 2 is proposed to add redeposits (automated ones from BetMGM and incentivized ones), move the Airtable operations cadence into Salesforce, and add the book assignment logic.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Phase two is where we're going to kind of introduce the redeposits uh both kind of like the automated ones that come with bit MGM MGM or like the the incentivized ones. Um this is where we're going to like really focus on air table um getting the operations um cadence being put into Salesforce

items.statement: Phase 3 is proposed to add payouts, payout line items, and additional reporting.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: and then with phase three would be um kind of adding the payouts the payout line items um and then any additional reporting that we're going to be adding

items.statement: Each release is proposed as its own contained package with no work bleeding from one phase into the next.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Each release here is like on its own package. / Waleed Alasadi: but there's no like we're not suggesting kind of bleed over work from one to the other.

items.statement: Waleed recommended pausing after Phase 1 to review before agreeing on Phase 2 and 3 details.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: but it would be a good idea before we agree on phase two and three to pause after phase one, decide what we like, what we don't like. / Waleed Alasadi: And we can discuss actually in detail what phase 2 would look like and then any onwards phases.

items.topic: Rep UX via list/console views, custom LWCs in native pages
items.statement: Rep experience covers list views and console views. Joyce's mockup resembles a Lightning page but is optimistic about native capability; best practice is custom LWCs inside native pages, not fully custom pages.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: So how do how do the sales reps interact with Salesforce list views, console views? That mockup that you sent us choice looks like a a lot like a lightning page. It is optimistic in some cases on like what Salesforce's native capability could do. Um so while I did say we can go native um we are able to like the best practice for us is to build custom LWC's um within the like within the like native page versus creating a whole new page that is entirely custom.

items.topic: Flag fraud buttons may need custom
items.statement: Buttons such as flag fraud might need small custom components, but native options also exist; to be discussed.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: I think you have like the flag um like flag fraud or something like that like those buttons like might might need to be a little custom but there are also native ways so we can discuss that

items.statement: Data migration of WagerTech's current Google Sheets is included in the proposed scope.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: doing data migration of the the the g the Google sheets that you currently have

items.topic: Rollout and rep training in scope
items.statement: Rollout and training the reps are included in the proposed scope, with weekly meetings with WagerTech.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: everything else from project management being able to kind of roll it out train the reps meeting with you on a weekly basis

items.statement: Proposed delivery model: one day-to-day primary consultant, with Waleed or Miko overseeing, attending weekly calls and active on a shared Slack channel. WagerTech uses Slack.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: However, we will have to have one primary consultant. That's going to be the day-to-day, the person like building, interacting with you. Um, either Mik or I will be overseeing it and we'll be in the weekly calls and kind of on the emails on the Slack channel. Do you use Slack? Perfect.

items.topic: Decommission old code; client help offered
items.statement: Jumpr expects to decommission the existing code as part of the build. Emily said WagerTech is open to picking up pieces of that work; Joyce clarified the in-house junior developer could help or ride along.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: I think like we're going to have to decommission the um the old code that you have like be able to build the objects like that sort of thing. / Emily Vandenberg: I think like you're saying decommission if there's any pieces that we can when we get deeper into this pickup as well to save on cost. I think we could be we'd like to be open to that conversation.

items.topic: Include junior developer Eric in meetings
items.statement: WagerTech's in-house junior developer (Eric) will be included in project meetings to ride along and support later enhancements.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: No, no, no. We're starting fresh. But I think um what you were talking about is like we have a junior developer in house who could help with some of that grunt work as well or at least like ride along / Waleed Alasadi: Yeah, absolutely. So, we can have that person included in our meetings. / Joyce Kiddell: Eric.

items.topic: Eric to learn Salesforce via Trailhead
items.statement: Waleed recommended that Eric start learning Salesforce on Trailhead and work toward Salesforce Administrator certification. No one was assigned to support this.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Okay. Um, he should definitely start learning Salesforce. So, there's Trailblazers. / Waleed Alasadi: and he should work towards becoming a a Salesforce administrator and then towards an advanced Salesforce

items.statement: The engagement must be approved by WagerTech's CEO; the three attendees are decision makers but not the final approver.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: you know, the three of us I would say are are definitely decision makers within the company, but ultimately we have to get this approved by our CEO.

items.statement: Waleed will send a concise follow-up email in a short format for the CEO, including the phase breakdown and an updated, more realistic timeline with reasons. Due most likely end of day, otherwise next morning; Emily said tomorrow is fine.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: How about I uh how about I I I send you this I send you a follow-up email once / Waleed Alasadi: I've done this and my email will be concise. / Joyce Kiddell: Yes. / Joyce Kiddell: if you can um include that in your email, like the summary email, and then maybe give us like an updated like more realistic timeline that you would / Waleed Alasadi: I'll tell you. Sorry. Most likely by end of day. If not by end of day, when you wake up tomorrow, you'll have the revised kind of
items.due: Most likely end of day 2026-06-03, otherwise morning of 2026-06-04

items.topic: Connect with data engineer after alignment
items.statement: Emily suggested that soon after alignment Jumpr connects with WagerTech's data engineer to find optimization in the first two work streams (project setup/design and object build).
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: I do think um in short order it would be good for our kind of data a connect thereafter once you know we're aligned to understand if there's any kind of optimization that's happening within those kind of first two work streams.

items.statement: Salesforce storage will run out and is expensive to extend. Options are buying more Salesforce storage or an external store such as AWS File Connect (upload in Salesforce, stored outside). Dropbox is not the cheapest option. Emily noted Jumpr raised no blocker.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: So, we're either going to and it's not cheap, but we can talk to them about it and you can do a comparison of the price for that versus like external sources. Um, Dropbox is definitely not the cheapest option out there and because you don't need the interface anymore. Um, we could possibly look at um like I I was saying earlier like AWS File Connect. / Waleed Alasadi: Only thing is Salesforce storage is expensive.

items.statement: Joyce suggested storage (including cold versus accessible storage) as an agenda item for the upcoming session with Straw.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um I feel like that's a good agenda item for when we connect with Straw because he has thoughts around storage too. like if we go cold or like still need it to be accessible.
items.asr_note: Straw = name unclear, possibly the data engineer [ASR?]

items.topic: Evaluate Platform licenses in design phase
items.statement: Jumpr raised moving most users to Salesforce Platform licenses instead of Enterprise Sales Cloud. WagerTech is on a one-year contract and is open to exploring; Waleed proposed treating it as a design-phase consideration, with any change at renewal. Some full licenses would still be needed (admins, data extraction).
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: if we have the opportunity to look maybe look back or, you know, see if we can pay at a different tier, we'd be open to at least exploring / Lina Ceniccola: We are on a year contract. / Waleed Alasadi: but since you're on a one year let's take that as a consideration as part of the design phase in the beginning and if we decide decide that that's the approach that they want to take then like this year it is what it is but we can talk to Salesforce about like the the next um kind of renewal and how they change into

items.topic: Platform license conflicts with person accounts
items.statement: On Platform licenses the Lead object is not available (needs a custom object) and Person Accounts cannot be used (revert to regular accounts); storage may also be affected. This conflicts with the proposed person-account model.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: The lead object, we'll have to come up with a make it into a custom object as well as not being able to use person accounts and having to revert to using regular accounts because that comes with platform. / Miko Sumagang: moved into like some something like else to stick around. Um there might be like some like repercussions like around storage as well.

items.statement: WagerTech's goal is simplicity without over-engineering so the team can maintain it, with core workflows set up as the first win.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: as long as we're kind of keeping it in focus of like simplicity and not over engineering this is like a key I think like a key goal in addition to some of the others to one ensure we can maintain and that it doesn't kind of become too complex / Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, I think like having our core workflows set up and that as a / Lina Ceniccola: win, we that's I mean our main goal here,

items.statement: Waleed asked WagerTech to consider stretching go-live past July for better outcomes. Joyce asked him to put an updated, more realistic timeline with reasons in the summary email so they can raise it.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: We've been waiting for too long. Stretching it a little bit, I think, will yield better outcomes if there's no real reason why we have to go live in / Joyce Kiddell: if you can um include that in your email, like the summary email, and then maybe give us like an updated like more realistic timeline that you would / Joyce Kiddell: prefer. um then we can always raise that but just give us good reasons behind it.
items.supersedes_hint: WagerTech's original July target (mid-July, tied to the Alberta launch)

items.topic: July deadline tied to Alberta launch
items.statement: The July deadline came from the plan to launch Salesforce with the Alberta market launch. Alberta runs the same way as other markets. Emily said July does not necessarily have to hold, but there was strong reason to start the new market with Salesforce.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: I'll just kind of say that the one thing we were running towards a pretty hard deadline of July because there was a significant launch I think we told you of Alberta and the original goal was to launch Salesforce with Alberta. / Waleed Alasadi: C can I ask you something with Alberta? Is it going to work the same way like every other market? / Emily Vandenberg: Yes.
items.critic_note: Statement softened: transcript ('I'm not saying that, you know, it has to we're still kind of like stuck on that, but there was kind of strong reason') does not clearly support 'not insisting on it'.

items.topic: Personal WhatsApp has no API integration
items.statement: Waleed noted that reps appear to use personal WhatsApp accounts, which do not have API integration. He explored bringing in N8N to read chats but did not reach a direction.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: not sure if you use business WhatsApp or personal. looking at the screen recording, it looked like personal WhatsApps. Um, which like didn't doesn't have AI integration. Um, sorry, not AI, API integration. Uh, but I also looked at like what it would what would happen if we like bring in N8N into the mix and like having start reading the chats and it's just like I just kept going into whatifs

items.statement: Phase 1 proposal includes attribution configuration: flows that link the records together and automate attribution, with some rules to be built.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: when we talk about the attribution configuration, this is really about kind of building the flows that can help us like link all of all of that together so it can automate them. There's some rules we need to put in um in here

items.statement: Phase 1 proposal includes working with WagerTech to get the sign-up API working, creating the sign-up record, deduplication, and the sign-up workflow.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Um, a big chunk is going to go to kind of working with you on getting the API working, being able to create the signup, being able to like look at um dup dduplication and that kind of signup workflow that I that I mentioned.

items.statement: Proposed project controls: a weekly sync on last week's work, next week's work and progress, with the project tracked in Asana and WagerTech invited for visibility.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: So on a weekly basis, first of all, you are able to get a sync where we're going to be talking about what we've done the previous week, what we're going to do the next week, um how well the project is progressing. It is all tracked in a sauna that you are also invited in so that you have visibility to

items.statement: Waleed said Jumpr's consultants want a real opinion on the ERD and to collaborate on finalizing the design. Joyce said WagerTech is totally aligned. This refines item -17 (data engineer owns the final outlook).
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: we would like to have like a real opinion especially our consultants on the erd and like be able to allow to kind of collaborate with you on finalizing the design because we want to make sure on the success of this platform when we're done. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, I think we're totally aligned to that.

items.topic: Client ERD maps entities and fields
items.statement: Joyce said the ERD maps all entities, fields and their relationships, and that whether each entity becomes a Salesforce object is not WagerTech's call. She expects the early design work to be validation rather than building from scratch.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: once you see the year ID like it's literally like all the different entities or like in terms of whether or not they're actually objects in Salesforce that's not our call but we have the entities mapped out and all the different fields and how they like speak to each other. / Joyce Kiddell: So, it's more of a validation versus um ideally building from

items.statement: Waleed raised an idea that going to Salesforce and starting fresh would save a lot, then parked the conversation. Joyce replied that they are starting fresh. It is not clear whether this means a new org or only not reusing code.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: we do have Mik and I have one thought about if you don't mind like going to Salesforce and starting fresh that would save us a lot if that makes sense. But we don't have to have let's not have that conversation now. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, that sounds good. / Joyce Kiddell: No, no, no. We're starting fresh.
items.asr_note: Mik = Miko [ASR]; meaning of 'going to Salesforce and starting fresh' unclear (possibly new org)

items.statement: Lina said the main goal now is core workflows and quick wins; other WagerTech businesses and workflows are future investments, not the current focus.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, I think like having our core workflows set up and that as a / Lina Ceniccola: win, we that's I mean our main goal here, but we definitely have, you know, other businesses and other workflows that we would want to invest in in the future.

items.topic: Client empowered for simple admin changes
items.statement: Waleed recommended that WagerTech be empowered to make simple changes such as adding a field, with Eric owning the org, subject to change management.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: you're a small company so yes Eric is going to own it and have something but yes there's something to be spoken about change management but you should be empowered to go and add a field because all of a sudden we need to track this

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: WhatsApp selected for notifications The team decided to utilize WhatsApp for system notifications instead of the native Salesforce app or email.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Joyce Kiddell: ... maybe that like we pivot that to just be like WhatsApp focused. / Waleed Alasadi: So and that that could happen absolutely like notifications to WhatsApp could happen.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary marks it ALIGNED/decided; transcript shows a tentative suggestion ('maybe') and 'could happen', with WhatsApp work also deferred out of Phase 1.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Dedicated WhatsApp Business account required The team committed to acquiring a dedicated WhatsApp Business account to handle notification delivery.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, we could get a WhatsApp business account dedicated to this.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary says 'committed'; Lina only said they 'could' get one.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Object model design approach accepted The team accepted the proposed object model design, which includes utilizing Person Accounts for players and referrers and the native User object for role management.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Waleed Alasadi: So, we can talk more about like this is not final. Obviously, in the first like week or so, we're going to finalize the design.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary says accepted; Waleed said it is not final, and Joyce later asked that the data engineer's ERD be the source of truth with the data engineer owning the final design.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Phased project delivery targets a late July launch to ensure high quality outcomes.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Waleed Alasadi: I know you mentioned middle of July. It is really tight ... I think July 31st or end of July. / Joyce Kiddell: ... maybe give us like an updated like more realistic timeline
gemini_disagreements.why: No launch target was agreed. Client asked for mid-July, Jumpr proposed end of July and then suggested going beyond July; an updated timeline is pending in the follow-up email.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: [Joyce Kiddell, Lina Ceniccola] Develop Internal Skills: Support Eric in completing Salesforce administrator training through the Trailhead system.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Waleed Alasadi: Okay. Um, he should definitely start learning Salesforce. So, there's Trailblazers. / Waleed Alasadi: and he should work towards becoming a a Salesforce administrator
gemini_disagreements.why: Waleed only recommended Trailhead; Joyce and Lina were not assigned any action.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Payment Processing and Banking Integration: Joyce Kiddell expressed interest in connecting fintech payment solutions or banking APIs directly with Salesforce. Waleed Alasadi agreed to research the feasibility of these connections, noting that a "bank transfer" object will be built
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Lina Ceniccola: We're also looking to explore the API connection with our current bank. So that's something to discuss in this scope too.
gemini_disagreements.why: Bank API request came from Lina, not Joyce (Joyce raised fintech processors as a down-the-line topic). 'Will be built' is firmer than the proposal stage of the meeting.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: A new signup workflow was defined where API integrations will create signup records ... subsequently converted to a person account (a "player") once verification steps, such as depositing funds, are completed
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Waleed Alasadi: Um, and then, um, if they are a lead, once we have like I don't know, we're gonna have to decide when that action happens, but likely once they send proof for the first deposit or what have you
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary presents the flow as defined and the conversion trigger as set; transcript shows a proposal with the trigger still to be decided.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: The team agreed to start the implementation from scratch, bypassing existing code to build a clean architecture using person accounts.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Waleed Alasadi: So, we can talk more about like this is not final. Obviously, in the first like week or so, we're going to finalize the design.
gemini_disagreements.why: Start-fresh was agreed, but person accounts were proposed as not final, and Platform licenses discussed later would remove person accounts.

notes: Pre-signature proposal walkthrough (post-discovery) of phases, object model and timeline. Rule 5: estimated hours, hourly rate, currency/sales tax, invoicing cadence, cost-range requests, Jumpr staffing/company details, proposal-update request, client license costs and retainer remarks were skipped (9 passages); Gemini summary items on those commercial topics were not assessed. A data engineer joined briefly at the end (unnamed). Next-step 'Provide References' omitted as non-delivery sales content.
critic_notes: Critic read all 653 lines. All 41 original quotes verified verbatim at stated lines. Added 9 items (-42 to -50), modified 3 (-41 statement softened; -11 and -15 summary_agreement set to no), added 3 Gemini disagreements. Rule 5 content (hours, rates, currency, tax, invoicing, staffing, retainer, license costs) not extracted.
